name: Nêlêmwa / nêlêmwa-nixumwak
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Bril, Isabelle. 2004. Noms composés en nêlêmwa. In Pierre Arnaud (ed.), Le Nom composé: Données sur 16 langues, 185-220. Lyon: Presses Universitaires de Lyon. Open-access author deposit HAL halshs-00006061 (https://shs.hal.science/halshs-00006061/document).
catalog_locator: p. 204, sec. 3 'Particularités morphologiques', second paragraph (HAL deposit halshs-00006061 of the PUL chapter)
catalog_quote: Voici d’abord quelques remarques sur l’accentuation des composés, puis un rappel sur les caractéristiques des diverses classes de noms, car celles-ci ont une influence sur la morphologie et les types de composés. L’accent porte généralement sur la syllabe initiale du radical des mots simples ou de chaque radical des composés, sauf si l’initiale du composé est un préfixe ou une forme courte assimilée à un préfixe. On oppose donc 'thaamwa 'laeo "femmes-esprits", qui a un accent sur chaque radical du composé, à kâ-'raamwa "génie féminin des airs", dont la syllabe initiale est la forme courte de kâxa "génie", c’est donc la syllabe initiale du radical (thaamwa "femme") qui est accentuée. De même, dans les cas suivants, chaque radical du composé est accentué: (ni) 'hâlûû 'bolaa "(à) l’ombre du bananier" (hâlûû-t "ombre" bolaa "bananier"), (ni yeewa-t) 'khuwo-'thaabwan "(lors du) dîner" (yeewa-t "temps" khuwo "nourriture" thaabwan "soir").
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: Stress generally falls on the initial syllable of the root of simple words, or of each root of compounds, except when the first element of the compound is a prefix or a short form assimilated to a prefix. Thus 'thaamwa 'laeo 'spirit-women', with a stress on each root of the compound, contrasts with kâ-'raamwa 'female air spirit', whose initial syllable is the short form of kâxa 'spirit'; it is therefore the initial syllable of the root (thaamwa 'woman') that is stressed. Likewise, in the following cases each root of the compound is stressed: (ni) 'hâlûû 'bolaa '(in) the shade of the banana tree' [...]
new_statements.citation: Bril, Isabelle. 2004. Noms composés en nêlêmwa. In Pierre Arnaud (ed.), Le Nom composé: Données sur 16 langues, 185-220. Lyon: Presses Universitaires de Lyon. (open on HAL: halshs-00006061)

On oppose donc 'thaamwa 'laeo.. à kâ-'raamwa.. c'est donc la syllabe initiale du radical (thaamwa) qui est accentuée. De même.. (ni) 'hâlûû 'bolaa.. (ni yeewa-t) 'khuwo-'thaabwan'. the compiler '[..]' only truncates the last example. p.207 (the text) also confirmed: old final (C)V 'ont disparu dans la forme libre du fait du déplacement de l'accent'. READING: I agree with…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Root-initial stress: the accent falls on the first syllable of the lexical root; prefixes and prefix-like reduced first elements of compounds are skipped (unstressed), so in prefixed words stress is on the first root syllable rather than the absolute word-initial syllable. In compounds each root keeps its own initial stress. For unprefixed simple words this amounts to word-initial stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed as such; in compounds each radical carries an accent ('thaamwa 'laeo, 'khuwo-'thaabwan) with no ranking of primary vs secondary given.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged with 'généralement'; prefixes and short (reduced) compound-initial forms assimilated to prefixes do not take the accent (kâ-'raamwa). p.207 also invokes a historical 'déplacement de l'accent' to explain loss of old final (C)V in free forms of some nouns.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement made in passing in a chapter on compound nouns (not a phonology chapter); covers simple words and compounds; author is the primary fieldworker/grammarian of the language (Bril 2000, 2002).
new_statements.identity_note: Bril's data are primarily the nêlêmwa variety (Poum, Tiabet, northern islets); nixumwak (Koumac) is described by her as differing only morpho-phonologically and lexically. The 2004 statement is given for 'nêlêmwa' without dialect qualification. Glottolog kuma1276 covers both (Nêlêmwa-Nixumwak, ISO nee); Haudricourt 1963 and Rivierre 1979 'Koumac' describe the nixumwak side.
